pois.wikipedia: en:History of the Jews in Estonia
pois.intro: The history of Jews in Estonia starts with reports of the presence of individual Jews in what is now Estonia from as early as the 14th century.

pois.name: Toompea loss
pois.intro: Toompea castle is a medieval castle on Toompea hill in the central part of Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. In modern times, it houses the Parliament of Estonia.

pois.name: Niguliste kirik
pois.intro: St. Nicholas Church is a medieval church building in Tallinn, Estonia.

pois.name: Kadrioru loss
pois.description: The constraction of the Kadriorg Palace was started by the Tsar Peter the Great of Russia in 1718. It was named Kadriorg (in German Catharinenthal) in honour of his wife Catherine I.
pois.intro: Kadriorg Palace is an 18th-century Petrine Baroque palace in Kadriorg, Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. Both the Estonian and the German names for the palace mean "Catherine's valley".

pois.name: Kumu kunstimuuseum
pois.intro: The Kumu Art Museum is an art museum in Tallinn, Estonia. It is one of the largest museums in Estonia and one of the largest art museums in Northern Europe.

pois.name: Raekoda
pois.intro: The Tallinn Town Hall is a building in the Old Town of Tallinn, Estonia, next to the Town Hall Square. The building is located in the south side of the medieval market square and is 36.8 metres long.

pois.name: Stenbocki maja
pois.intro: Stenbock House is a prominent neo-classical building located on Toompea hill, Tallinn. It is the official seat of the Government of Estonia.

pois.name: Vabaduse väljak
pois.intro: Freedom Square is a plaza on the southern end of the Old Town in Tallinn, Estonia, where state functions and various concerts take place. It is bounded on the east by St.

pois.name: Pikk Hermann
pois.intro: Pikk Hermann is a tower of the Toompea Castle, on Toompea hill in Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. The first part of the tower was built in 1360–1370.

pois.name: Tallinna teletorn
pois.intro: Tallinn TV Tower is a free-standing structure with an observation deck, built to provide better telecommunication services for the 1980 Moscow Summer Olympics regatta event. It is located near the suburb Pirita, six km north-east of the Tallinn city center.

pois.name: Kiek in de Kök
pois.openingHours: May-Sep Mo-Su 11:00-18:00; Oct-Apr Tu-Su 11:00-18:00; PH off
pois.intro: Kiek in de Kök is an artillery tower in Tallinn, Estonia, built in 1475. It gained the name Kiek in de Kök from the ability of tower occupants to see into kitchens of nearby houses.

pois.name: Eesti Meremuuseum
pois.intro: The Estonian Maritime Museum is located in the Fat Margaret tower in the old town of Tallinn. The museum presents the history of ships and navigation in Estonia and related to Estonia.

pois.name: Tallinna loomaaed
pois.intro: Tallinn Zoo is a zoo in Tallinn, Estonia, that was founded in 1939. It is the only zoo in Estonia, and as of 2012, it housed 13,336 animals representing 548 species.

pois.name: Paks Margareeta
pois.intro: Fat Margaret is a tower in Tallinn, Estonia. Nowadays, the tower is home to Estonian Maritime Museum.

pois.name: Raekoja plats
pois.intro: Raekoja plats is a town square beside Tallinn Town Hall in the center of the Tallinn Old Town in Tallinn, Estonia. It is a venue for numerous small festivals or concerts like Tallinn Old Town Days, and several bars and restaurants are located in the near vicinity.

pois.name: Pirita klooster
pois.intro: Pirita Convent was a Bridgettine convent for both nuns and monks, located in the district of Pirita in Tallinn, Estonia. It functioned from 1407 to 1575.

pois.name: Eesti Ajaloomuuseum
pois.intro: Estonian History Museum is a museum about the history of Estonia in Tallinn. It was initially established by the pharmacist Johann Burchart, who ran the town hall pharmacy known as the Raeapteek.

pois.name: Eesti Loodusmuuseum
pois.intro: The Estonian Museum of Natural History is the Estonian national museum for natural history. It is situated in Tallinn's Old Town.

pois.name: Okupatsioonide muuseum
pois.intro: The Vabamu or Vabamu Museum of Occupations and Freedom tells the history of Estonia during and after the Soviet and Nazi occupations, arriving at the era of restoration of independence. The museum is located at the corner of Toompea St.

pois.name: Eesti Arhitektuurimuuseum
pois.intro: Estonian Museum of Architecture is an architecture museum in Tallinn, Estonia. It is located in the Rotermann quarter.

pois.name: Mikkeli muuseum
pois.intro: The Mikkel Museum is a branch of the Art Museum of Estonia, located in Kadriorg park in Tallinn. It displays a collection of mainly Western art and ceramics, and Chinese porcelain, donated by art collector Johannes Mikkel in 1994.

pois.name: Tallinna Linnamuuseum
pois.intro: Tallinn City Museum is a city museum in Tallinn, Estonia. The museum was founded in 1937 as Historic Museum of the City of Tallinn.

pois.name: Olde Hansa
pois.intro: Olde Hansa is a restaurant in the Old Town in central Tallinn, Estonia, located in the protected Pakkhoone building.

pois.name: Peppersack
pois.description:
Meist ja meie ajaloost

Restoran Peppersack asub huvitava ajalooga majas, Tallinna vanalinna südames, Raekoja platsi vahetus läheduses.
pois.intro: Der Peppersack ist ein denkmalgeschütztes Gebäude in der estnischen Hauptstadt Tallinn. Das Haus wird als Gaststätte genutzt.

pois.name: Maiasmokk
pois.intro: Maiasmokk is a historical café in Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. In its current form it dates back to 1864, making it the oldest operational café in Estonia.

pois.name: Restoran MOON
pois.intro: Kohvik Moon is a restaurant in Tallinn, Estonia, located near the Viking Line harbour. The restaurant focuses on slavic food.

pois.name: Elevant
pois.description: Tallinn's best traditional Indian restaurant with wide selection for all tastes - we have meat, vegetable and vegan dishes.

pois.name: Ülemiste keskus
pois.intro: Ülemiste Keskus is a shopping centre in Tallinn, Estonia. It's adjacent to Tallinn Airport in Ülemiste.

pois.name: T1 keskus
pois.intro: T1 Tallinn is a shopping mall in Tallinn, Estonia. T1 calls itself as "Estonia’s first next-generation shopping and entertainment centre".

pois.name: Artius
pois.intro: Artius is a shopping centre in the centre of Tallinn, Estonia. Artius has a gross leasable area of 2,500 square metres containing 28 different shops, including women's fashion, footwear, kid's clothes, jewelry, cosmetics and beauty products.

pois.name: Kristiine keskus
pois.intro: Kristiine Centre is a shopping centre in Tallinn, Estonia. It's situated in Kristiine district's subdistrict of Lilleküla.

pois.name: oma asi d_sign
pois.description: Oma Asi Design Store is one of the best known concept gift shops in Tallinn. Fun, quirky and different gifts for locals and tourists. Ideal presents for special occasions or momentos to remember your visit to Tallinn which are slightly more imaginative.

pois.name: Tallinna Botaanikaaed
pois.intro: Tallinn Botanic Garden, is a botanical garden in Tallinn, Estonia. It is located on the right bank of the Pirita River, in the Kloostrimetsa forest in Pirita district.

pois.name: Lennusadam
pois.intro: The Seaplane Harbour is a maritime museum in Tallinn, Estonia, which opened in spring 2012. The museum is part of the Estonian Maritime Museum.

pois.name: Kadrioru park
pois.intro: Kadriorg Park is a park in Kadriorg, Tallinn, Estonia. Its area is about 70 ha.

pois.name: Taani kuninga aed
pois.intro: Danish King's Garden is a park in Tallinn Old Town, Estonia. The park is the place where the flag of Denmark, Dannebrog, according to tradition, is said to have been born.

pois.name: Musumägi
pois.intro: Virumägi, även Musumägi, är en liten kulle i början av Viru tänav i Tallinn i Estland. Den var ursprungligen en bastion, byggd i början av 1700-talet på svenska tiden.

pois.name: Hirvepark
pois.intro: Hirvepark is a park in Tallinn, Estonia. On 23 August 1987, the anti-Soviet Hirvepark meeting took place in the park.

pois.name: Noblessneri sadam
pois.intro: Noblessner is a harbour and former industrial area in the northern district of Tallinn, Estonia. Since 2013 it has been redeveloped into a cultural and residential area with a museum, art centre, craft brewery, marina, seafront promenade and cafes and restaurants.

pois.name: Kalasadam
pois.intro: Le port de pêche est un port de passagers situé dans la baie de Tallinn à Tallinn en Estonie.

pois.name: Pikakari rand
pois.intro: La plage Pikakari est une plage de baignade de Tallinn en Estonie.

pois.name: Pirita jõeoru maastikukaitseala
pois.intro: Pirita River Valley Landscape Conservation Area is a nature park which is located in Harju County, Estonia. The area of the nature park is 707 ha.

pois.intro: Patarei on Tallinnassa sijaitseva entinen keskusvankila.

pois.intro: Le phare avant de Tallinn est un feu situé dans l'arrondissement de Lasnamäe à Tallinn dans le Comté de Harju, en Estonie, sur le golfe de Finlande. Il fonctionne conjointement avec le phare arrière de Tallinn qui se trouve à 1.1 km plus au nord.

pois.intro: Le phare arrière de Tallinn est un feu situé dans l'arrondissement de Lasnamäe à Tallinn dans le Comté de Harju, en Estonie, sur le golfe de Finlande. Il fonctionne conjointement avec le phare avant de Tallinn qui se trouve à 1.1 km plus au sud.

pois.name: EML Lembit
pois.intro: EML Lembit is one of two Kalev-class mine-laying submarines built for the Republic of Estonia before World War II, and is now a museum ship in Tallinn. She was launched in 1936 at Vickers-Armstrongs, Barrow-in-Furness, and served in the Estonian Navy and the Soviet Navy.

pois.name: Maarjamäe loss
pois.intro: Maarjamäe Palace is a building in Maarjamäe, Tallinn. The palace is located at the site of the earlier Maarjamäe summer manor, which is its main building.

pois.name: Roheline turg
pois.intro: Der Grüne Markt ist eine Grünanlage in der estnischen Hauptstadt Tallinn.

pois.name: Järve keskus
pois.intro: Järve Centre is a shopping centre in southern Tallinn, Estonia. Järve Centre is the biggest shopping centre selling furnishing goods in Estonia, with a gross leasable area of 43,000 square metres containing nearly 111 different shops.

pois.name: Rocca al Mare kaubanduskeskus
pois.intro: Rocca al Mare Shopping Centre is a shopping centre in Tallinn, Estonia. It is situated in Haabersti, Haabersti District.
